titles.title: JediAcademy
titles.engine:
id Tech 3 (Raven), retail 1.01.
- jasp.exe 'JA: v1.0.1.0' (SP; the UI is compiled into the exe).
- jamp.exe 'JAmp: v1.0.1.0' (MP; uix86.dll, cgamex86 and jampgamex86 come from base/assets3.pk3).
- Both register r_mode with a plain 3-argument Cvar_Get, so there is no range clamp.
- The engine table covers modes 0-12 (11 = 856x480, 12 = 2400x600 surround). There is no 1920x1080 entry, so 1080p exists only through r_mode -1.
titles.launch_sets:
Mechanism (confirmed):
- 'Play Jedi Academy.bat' and 'Play Jedi Academy - Multiplayer.bat' differ only in GAME=jasp/jamp.
- Both call FLEETRES.BAT and write base\fleetres.cfg: r_mode "-1", r_customwidth %FR_W%, r_customheight %FR_H%, r_customaspect 1, r_customPixelAspect 1, r_fullscreen 1, r_displayRefresh %FR_HZ%, cg_fov %FR_FOV%. The same values go on the command line as +set.
- base\autoexec.cfg ends 'exec fleetres.cfg' and sets no r_mode.
- The agent writes the same body at sync time (gameres.h rule {JediAcademy, base\fleetres.cfg, NULL}).
- The staged FLEETRES.EXE md5 bb180f3b... matches provisioning/fleetres. `stage-fleetres.py --check` (re-run): 213 current, 1 failure (Thief2 only).

Result: 1920x1080 fullscreen on any LCD box where the disc mounts and the EDID is read. Measured on .145 for both jasp and jamp (PER-TITLE-STATUS).

Correction for .123: it is no longer gated.
- HWPROFILE now reports disc_mount=true (d347bus); wmic shows a DAEMON Tools drive D:.
- 'Jedi Academy.lnk' and 'Jedi Academy - Multiplayer.lnk' are both on its All Users desktop.
- Its GAMESYNC-written base\fleetres.cfg says r_mode -1 / 1920 / 1080, and GAMERES targets 1920x1080.
- Not launched: the box was busy with other agents' tests.

New for .240: the EDID is read again (DELL E2313H, target 1920x1080, fleetres.cfg r_mode -1 1920x1080), but disc mounting is broken there right now.
- At 04:51 box time the SoF2 SP launcher (same fleet disc-mount template, same DAEMON Tools unit 0) wrote 'MOUNT FAILED - started against an unrelated disc'.
- F: holds STARCRAFT, mounted at every logon by the HKLM Run value 'StarCraftCD'.
- So on .240 the JKA shortcuts will very likely stop at 'Disk 1 not in drive'. This is inferred from the same template; the JKA launcher itself was not re-run.

.195 (Win7, WinCDEmu): GAMERES target is 1920x1080; not re-measured.
titles.menu_source:
A hardcoded cvarFloatList on ui_r_mode, the same in four files:
- assets1 ui/setup.menu
- assets1 ui/ingamesetup.menu
- assets3 ui/jamp/setup.menu (the 1.01 copy, overrides assets1's)
- assets1 ui/jamp/ingame_setup.menu

The list: {640x480 3, 800x600 4, 1024x768 6, 1152x864 7, 1280x1024 8, 1600x1200 9, 2048x1536 10, 2400x600 12}. On open, 'uiScript getvideosetup' copies r_mode into ui_r_mode; on Apply, 'updatevideosetup' copies it back and runs vid_restart. There is no 1920x1080 entry and no -1 entry. The second item named video_mode in each file is an anisotropic-filtering slider, not a second list. The Setup menu opens on the 'video' group in both SP and MP (onOpen 'show video').

With the launcher's r_mode -1, the Video Mode line shows EMPTY, not 'Custom':
- Item_Multi_Setting returns "" when nothing matches: jasp.exe function 0x4A0BB0 returns 0x5037A0 (a NUL byte); 1.01 uix86.dll function 0x4001CB50 returns 0x40032D93 (a NUL byte).
- No '@MENUS_CUSTOM' literal exists in jasp, jamp or uix86.

The Video Quality presets (ui_r_glCustom) also write ui_r_mode 4 or 3 (uix86 0x4000B706/B7AB/B84D/B8E6; the same pattern in jasp.exe). So picking a preset and pressing Apply drops the game to 800x600 or 640x480.

Evidence directory: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/review-jka-sof2-rtcw/

Checked from the prior agent's evidence (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/idtech3-jka-sof2-rtcw/): jka-menu-modelists.txt, engine-mode-tables.txt, binaries.txt.

Re-checked by me:
- The menu files (extracted from assets1/assets3).
- No .cfg inside assets0-3 sets r_mode.
- The three fleet servers' live server.cfg files all run sv_pure 0. jka-server is OpenJK openjkded on :29070, protocol 26.
- A share-wide case-insensitive find (depth 8) found no JKA fix payload.
titles.fix:
Unchanged in substance: the renderer already runs r_mode -1 at the panel size, so only the menus need changing.

1. Stage base\zz_fleet_video.pk3, which sorts after assets3.pk3. It holds edited copies of four menus:
   - ui/setup.menu and ui/ingamesetup.menu (from assets1)
   - ui/jamp/setup.menu (from assets3, the 1.01 copy)
   - ui/jamp/ingame_setup.menu (from assets1)
2. In each video_mode cvarFloatList, add `@MENUS_CUSTOM -1`. The "Custom" string exists in MENUS.str, and the JKA parser accepts a negative value.
3. Optionally add two read-only text items, or ITEM_TYPE_EDITFIELD items, for r_customwidth and r_customheight in the 'video' group.

With that, the line reads 'Custom' on every box at the size FLEETRES wrote (1920x1080 on the four LCDs). Do not label the -1 entry literally '1920 X 1080': on the CRT boxes it means 1024x768.

No launcher or gameres.h change is needed.
titles.fix_source:
Already in the tree: base/assets1.pk3 and base/assets3.pk3; nothing needs downloading.

I re-ran the share search case-insensitively at depth 8 across /mnt/retro-share/Files, excluding Games-Library. It found only the two retail ISOs (Games/Windows XP/Star Wars Jedi Knight - Jedi Academy/JediAcademy-CD1.iso and -CD2.iso). There is no JKA widescreen or menu fix and no XP-capable OpenJK build. Per the tree's README-FLEET.txt, OpenJK's prebuilt binaries are subsystem 6.0 with VC140 imports.
titles.fix_risk:
Low: client-side data only.
- Multiplayer: jka-server runs sv_pure 0, so the pk3 stays loaded while connected.
- A .menu syntax error silently breaks that whole menu, so check SP and MP, main and in-game.
- Using the assets1 copy of ui/jamp/setup.menu would undo the 1.01 menu changes.
- GAMESYNC never deletes, so a rollback needs a launcher-side delete.
- The launcher rewrites fleetres.cfg at every start, so an in-menu pick does not survive the next launch (by design).
- New: the Video Quality presets write ui_r_mode 4 or 3 in code (uix86.dll and jasp.exe). A player who picks a preset and applies drops to 800x600 or 640x480 until the next launch. A menu-only fix cannot stop that.
- The HUD and menus stay 640x480-virtual, stretched to 16:9 (engine limit).
titles.hw_check:
Use .145 or .123: both XP, where GDI captures fullscreen, and both have DAEMON Tools. Avoid .240 until its unit-0 mount works (F: = STARCRAFT from the StarCraftCD Run key). Use .195 only for WINLIST, not frames (Win7).

1. EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\JediAcademy" "Play Jedi Academy.bat", and the same for the Multiplayer .bat.
2. WINLIST must show the jasp or jamp window at 0,0 1920x1080.
3. Main menu > SETUP opens on the Video group. Today the Video Mode value is blank. After the fix it must read 'Custom' (with 1920/1080 if the fields are added), and cycling must come back to it.

The menus are relative-mouse, so cycling needs a person. To at least see the line, relaunch jasp windowed (+set r_fullscreen 0) and type 'uimenu setupMenu' at the console (synthetic keys only reach a window), screenshot it, then confirm fullscreen again.
titles.verifier_notes:
Changed:
1. REFUTED: '.123 has no mounter, both shortcuts suppressed'. .123 now reports disc_mount true (d347bus), has a DAEMON Tools drive D:, and carries both JKA desktop shortcuts. Its fleetres.cfg targets 1920x1080.
2. ADDED: .240 is currently blocked by a failed DAEMON Tools mount (the StarCraft image is mounted at logon; the same launcher template failed at 04:51 tonight). The JKA effect there is inferred, not re-run.
3. CONFIRMED statically, and made precise: the Video Mode line is blank (not 'Custom') under r_mode -1 in both SP and MP. Item_Multi_Setting returns a pointer to "" (addresses above).
4. ADDED risk: the Video Quality presets overwrite ui_r_mode with 4 or 3.

Everything else was confirmed: the four menu lists, the engine tables, the launcher and fleetres.cfg bodies, the gameres rule, the FLEETRES md5, the stage-fleetres check, and sv_pure 0 on jka-server. No JKA process was launched in this review.

titles.title: SoldierOfFortune2
titles.engine:
Raven id Tech 3 (Team Arena-era menus), two engines:
- sof2mp.exe 'SOF2MP GOLD V1.03' (MP, md5 0263922b...): image base 0x400000, game directory base\mp, config base\MP\sof2mp.cfg, UI vm/sof2mp_ui.qvm from update103.pk3.
- SoF2.exe (SP, md5 c0c87332...): image base 0x10000000, which is why its addresses read 0x100xxxxx. Config base\sof2sp.cfg; RMF menus.

Both mode tables run 0-11 (11 = 856x480) with no 1920x1080. Neither exe carries SafeDisc (discprotect.py).
titles.launch_sets:
Result: a 4:3 index mode.
- r_mode 7 (1152x864) on .123, .145 and .240.
- r_mode 6 (1024x768) on .195: its GAMERES mode list has no 1152x864, so q3mode is 6.
- Measured tonight on .240: DISPLAYCFG read 1152x864 while the SP launcher's SoF2.exe ran.

Mechanism (confirmed):
- Both launchers call FLEETRES.BAT and write the shared base\fleetres.cfg.
- MP writes: r_mode %FR_Q3MODE%, r_fullscreen 1, r_displayRefresh, cg_fov %FR_FOV%. The SP launcher's copy also has r_customaspect and r_customPixelAspect.
- Both pass +set r_mode %FR_Q3MODE% +set r_fullscreen 1 +set cg_fov %FR_FOV%.
- MP reads base\MP\autoexec.cfg, which reaches base\fleetres.cfg through the search path. SP reads base\autoexec.cfg.
- The agent writes the 'idtech3-index' body at sync time.

Correction on cg_fov: the MP cgame (update103 sof2mp_cgame.qvm) registers cg_fov with flags 0x2001 and range 80..100. In game the launcher's 106 becomes 100; sof2mp.cfg on .145 and .240 both read cg_fov "100" after play. The 'hor+ FOV on a 4:3 render' is therefore 100, not 106.

Shortcuts: MP clears disc_mount per shortcut. The SP shortcut needs sofii_1 and now exists on .123 too. On .240 the SP mount failed tonight, so SP fell back to the StarCraft disc on F:.
titles.menu_source:
MP: ui/setup_display.menu, item 'videomode_multi', bound directly to r_mode. The list: {512*384 2, 640*480 3, 800*600 4, 960*720 5, 1024*768 6, 1152*864 7, 1280*1024 8, 1600*1200 9}.
- The update101.pk3 copy wins over mp.pk3's.
- Correction: the two files are NOT identical (update101 adds a Vertical Sync item). Only the mode list is the same, so any override must start from the update101 copy.

SP: therest.pk3 menus/m_video.rmf, `match "3,4,6,7,8,9"`, with labels from Strip/menu_video.sp. video_init.cfg does set menu_mode $r_mode; video_apply.cfg does set r_mode $menu_mode.

MP UI presets (now confirmed by disassembling sof2mp_ui.qvm 1.03): the four graphics presets call trap syscall -7 (Cvar_SetValue) with r_mode 4, 3, 3 and 3. The UI has no vmCvar-table registration of r_mode.

titles.fix:
Multiplayer: the binary patch is now VERIFIED on hardware.
- In the staged sof2mp.exe, change file offset 0xBA61A-0xBA61D from 00 00 40 40 (3.0f) to 00 00 80 BF (-1.0f). Only 0xBA61C and 0xBA61D actually change.
- Cvar_Get takes min and max only from the first registration that carries flag 0x2000 (the renderer's), so nothing later can re-impose 3.

Then, in lockstep:
1. Move SoF2 back to the standard idiom: the MP launcher, the SP launcher, stage-fleetres.py (drop it from IDTECH3_NO_CUSTOM_MODE) and the gameres.h rule (idtech3-index becomes the NULL/custom body). tests/python/test_gameres_mirror.py must stay green, or the two writers fight over base\fleetres.cfg.
2. Add a `"Custom" -1` entry to update101's ui/setup_display.menu, in a pk3 that sorts last in base\ (or base\mp).

cg_fov: sending 106 is harmless, but the cgame clamps it to 100.

Single player (VERIFIED: SoF2.exe honours r_mode -1 at 1920x1080 with no patch):
- If the MP exe is patched, the shared standard body covers both engines.
- If it is not patched, the SP launcher must put -1 and FR_W/FR_H in an SP-only cfg exec'd from base\autoexec.cfg (MP's base\MP\autoexec.cfg shadows that file). Never put -1 in the shared base\fleetres.cfg while MP is unpatched: stock MP clamps it to 640x480, as S1 shows.
- SP menu: extend m_video.rmf to `match "3,4,6,7,8,9,-1"` and VIDMODES with ',Custom' (untested).
titles.fix_source:
The patch bytes are derived from the staged sof2mp.exe and were tested as a temp copy on .240. Menu sources are already in the tree: base/update101.pk3 (ui/setup_display.menu, Strip/menu_video.sp) and base/therest.pk3 (menus/m_video.rmf).

A share-wide case-insensitive search (depth 8) found no SoF2 fix; the share has only the retail and repack media, SoF2Demo.exe and Game Updates/sof2goldfull.exe. The PCGamingWiki community MP widescreen patch (file 1141) is not on the share and its contents are unverified.
titles.fix_risk:
Patched MP exe:
- The retail binary is modified; keep the original under _patches.
- The PE CheckSum is 0 and there is no SafeDisc, so the binary does not check itself.
- The size is unchanged, so GAMESYNC only propagates it if the mtime changes: publish through gvfs, not smbclient (which stamps Oct 2007).
- PunkBuster is off at both ends and the fleet sof2-server runs sv_pure 0.
- Q3-family servers check pk3s, not the client exe. The render was proven; a server join with the patched exe was NOT tested.
- Confirmed: the MP UI's graphics presets set r_mode 4 or 3, so picking one leaves 1080p until the next launch.
- The 640x480-virtual HUD and menus stretch at 16:9.
- cg_fov stays capped at 100.

SP:
- The first SP launch on every box stops at a modal 'New Video card detected' message box. The mode survives it (the scalability configs never set r_mode), but someone has to click OK once.
- RMF parsing of a -1 list value is untested.
titles.hw_check:

2. base\MP\qconsole.log (+set logfile 2) must read '...setting mode -1: 1920 1080 FS', and WINLIST must show 'SoF2 MP' at 0,0-1920x1080. This was already proven on .240 with a temp copy.
3. Join 192.168.1.132:20100 once, to prove the patched client still connects.
4. Main > SETUP > Display > 'Video Mode:' must show the new entry. The menus are relative-mouse, so a person has to cycle the item.

SP (.145 or .123; NOT .240 until its DAEMON Tools unit-0 mount works):
1. Launch with -1. The log must read 'MODE: -1, 1920 x 1080'.
2. On a box never run before, answer the 'New Video card detected' box, then confirm the mode after the re-init.
titles.verifier_notes:
Changed:
1. SP -1 support and the MP clamp were confirmed ON HARDWARE (.240). Stock MP with -1 comes up at 640x480; the patched copy at 1920x1080; SP at 1920x1080.
2. The patch is proven for rendering. Only 2 bytes differ, and min/max are latched from the renderer's registration.
3. CORRECTED cg_fov: the MP cgame clamps it to 80..100, so '106 on 16:9' is 100 in game and 'keep 106' is moot.
4. CORRECTED 'update101 setup_display.menu identical to mp.pk3': the files differ; the lists match.
5. RESOLVED an 'unknown': the MP UI presets set r_mode 4/3, and the UI does not register r_mode in its cvar table.
6. ADDED: SP's first-run 'Redetecting settings due to video card change' plus the modal dialog.
7. ADDED: the .240 mount failure and .123 gaining a mounter.

Confirmed: the launch mechanism, and FR_Q3MODE 7 or 6 per box.

State: .240 was restored (configs md5-identical, the temp exe and logs deleted). The launcher's failure path had taskkilled daemon.exe; I restarted it with its Run-key command line.

titles.title: ReturnToCastleWolfenstein
titles.engine:
id Tech 3 (Gray Matter/Nerve), GOG build 2.0.0.2:
- WolfSP.exe 'Wolf 1.32' (May 1 2002; its table covers 0-12, 12 = 1920x1200).
- WolfMP.exe 'Wolf 1.4-MP' (1.41; its table covers 0-11).
- UIs: uix86.dll (SP) and Main\ui_mp_x86.dll (MP).
- Configs: Main\wolfconfig.cfg and Main\wolfconfig_mp.cfg.

Both engines register r_mode with a plain 3-argument Cvar_Get and do not range-check it. Both now honour r_mode -1 on hardware. Neither exe carries SafeDisc.
titles.launch_sets:
Result (confirmed):
- 1152x864 (r_mode 7) on .123, .145 and .240.
- 1024x768 (r_mode 6) on .195.

Mechanism: all four launchers call FLEETRES.BAT and write Main\fleetres.cfg (r_mode %FR_Q3MODE%, r_fullscreen 1, r_displayRefresh, no cg_fov), passing +set r_mode %FR_Q3MODE% +set r_fullscreen 1. Main\autoexec.cfg execs fleetres.cfg. The agent writes 'idtech3-index-nofov' at sync.

The first-run exception is now REPRODUCED ON HARDWARE (.240, F1): with no Main\wolfconfig_mp.cfg (the state of a freshly synced tree) and the launcher's own args:
1. The log reads 'setting mode 7: 1152 864 FS'.
2. Then 'Found high quality video and CPU', 'execing highVidhighCPU.cfg', 'r_mode will be changed upon restarting'.
3. Then 'setting mode 3: 640 480 FS'; the window ends at 640x480.
4. The config it writes says r_mode "3" and com_recommendedSet "1". That is exactly the .246 symptom recorded in stage-fleetres.py.

The premise 'r_mode -1 does not exist in this engine' (launcher comments, gameres.h and IDTECH3_NO_CUSTOM_MODE) is FALSE on hardware, for both SP and MP.
titles.menu_source:
A hardcoded cvarFloatList bound directly to r_mode: {640 3, 800 4, 960 5, 1024 6, 1152 7, 1280x1024 8, 1600 9, 2048 10, 856x480 wide 11}.
- SP: sp_pak3.pk3 ui/system.menu and ui/ingame_system.menu (these override sp_pak1).
- MP: ui_mp/system.menu and ui_mp/ingame_system.menu exist ONLY in mp_pak1.pk3; mp_pak3 and mp_pak5 update ui_mp/menus.txt only.
- No list has 1920x1080. WolfSP's engine mode 12 (1920x1200) is in no menu.

The MP UI presets rewrite r_mode (confirmed in ui_mp_x86.dll at 0x4000D2A6, 0x4000D372 and 0x4000D4FB: r_mode 4, 3, 3).

Correction to the prior claim that ioRTCW 'ships the same stock menus'. ioRTCW 1.51c's MP UI (mp_bin0.pk3 vm/ui.mp.qvm) replaces ANY r_mode multi item's list with a built-in 32-entry list, which includes '1920x1080 (16:9)' as r_mode 26, 'Automatic (Native)' as -2 and 'Custom' as -1. Its SP ui_sp_x86.dll carries the same labels. The fleet's RTCW server is already ioRTCW 1.51c.

Static: static-rtcw.txt covers the ioRTCW built-in list and its r_mode hook, the retail preset writes, the menu file locations, and the Knightmare 1.42d PE and SSE2 audit.

Also: hardware-results-240.txt; 240-before/240-after (all configs restored, md5 OK); and the prior agent's rtcw-r_mode-and-first-run.disasm.txt, rtcw-menu-modelists.txt and rtcw-sp-1.42d-patch.txt (re-checked).
titles.fix:
1. Stop the first-run pass on both engines: `+set com_recommendedSet 1` on all four launchers' command lines, or a seta in the staged Main\autoexec.cfg. VERIFIED by F2.

2. Render at the panel size (VERIFIED for SP and MP): switch all four launchers, stage-fleetres.py (remove RTCW from IDTECH3_NO_CUSTOM_MODE) and gameres.h ('idtech3-index-nofov' becomes a custom-mode body) together, to r_mode -1 + r_customwidth %FR_W% + r_customheight %FR_H%. Keep test_gameres_mirror green so the two writers of Main\fleetres.cfg agree. SP and MP share that file, so both must take the same idiom.

3. Menus, retail route:
   - MP: a pk3 that sorts last in Main\, holding mp_pak1's ui_mp/system.menu and ingame_system.menu with `"Custom" -1` added.
   - SP: either the same edit of sp_pak3's two menus, or Knightmare's 1.42d from the share. For 1.42d, copy its WolfSP.exe and the three DLLs to the tree root, stage its pk3 as Main\sp_pak4b.pk3 (never over the staged 15 MB sp_pak4.pk3), and it lists '1920*1080 WS' (26) and 'Custom' (-1) with width/height fields.

4. Alternative worth a box test: the ioRTCW 1.51c client already on the share. Its UI injects '1920x1080 (16:9)', 'Automatic (Native)' (-2) and 'Custom' into the Video Mode list with no menu edits, and cg_fixedAspect 2 gives a widescreen-correct HUD. It needs +set fs_homepath pointed at the tree; its default is My Documents\RTCW, the per-user shadowing trap. It would best be added as extra shortcuts rather than replacing the retail launchers.

- Knightmare SP 1.42d: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Game Updates/RTCW/rtcw-sp-1.42d-win32-bin.zip (md5 482be194a3ebf4d0c1eb9ca664834838).
- ioRTCW 1.51c: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Game Updates/iortcw-1.51c-win-x86.zip, and /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games/Mods & Patches/iortcw-1.51c-mp-ready.zip (the latter was not in the prior survey).

titles.fix_risk:
com_recommendedSet 1: the preset pass is skipped, so picmip and similar settings stay at engine defaults. Harmless.

The -1 idiom:
- The retail HUD and menus are 640x480-virtual and stretch at 16:9.
- At the default cg_fov 90 the view is vert-.
- The MP UI presets reset r_mode to 4 or 3 for that session.
